transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-08 15:00 PDT / Duration 52m / Attendees: Samira Patel, Ethan Ruiz (Redwood); Priya Menon, James Holloway, Maya Lin, Liam O'Connor (Solaris)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes, quick agenda — renewal term, apac burst, brief security Qs, bench plan. Uh will kick it over to Priya for priorities.
[00:22] Priya: Yeah thanks Samira. So main ask, we want to extend for another year, but we need a ramp that covers peak underwriting windows in APAC. Right now latency in ap-northeast is a little high when we hit concurrent jobs, so need either reserved pool in ap-northeast-1 or a global burst option. Also: KMS integration, audit logs — James will cover legal timing.
[00:45] James: Yep, procurement timeline is tight. We need to get commercial terms by Friday, then legal review. Also our security team insists on customer-managed keys for any PII-related inference.
[01:05] Ethan: Cool — from a performance side, can you give ballpark RPS or tokens per second on those peak windows? That helps pick between Dedicated vs Hosted with burst.
[01:21] Priya: Peaks are around 600 qps for short 10–15 minute bursts during morning batch runs, avg day is like 35 qps. Payload size variable, about 300–600 tokens per inference on the underwriting model.
[01:40] Samira: Got it. So two levers: dedicated reserved capacity for predictable tail latency, or hosted with burst credits (cheaper off-peak) — we can model cost. Ethan, quick thought?
[01:55] Ethan: If bursts are frequent we recommend reserved capacity sized for common peak floor, with burst headroom. Our recent customers do hybrid: reserved baseline in ap-northeast + short burst pool shared across regions. That keeps P95 latency under 300ms for the sequence lengths you mentioned.
[02:18] Maya: Sorry can I jump — when you say P95 300ms is that token latency or end-to-end? Our stack adds a couple hundred ms for pre/post processing and VPC hops.
[02:31] Ethan: Good call — 300ms was model token generation time. End-to-end you'll see ~600–800ms depending on VPC NAT and middleware. We can reduce by colocating the VPC and using our private path (direct peering).
[02:49] Priya: Is the private path the VPC peering option? We saw notes about "V-P-C peering" in the docs but the team misread it as VPC cash in the memos, haha.
[03:03] Samira: (laughs) yeah that's a common transcribe error — it's VPC peering. We support VPC peering and private control plane for Private deployments; for hosted we do transit via encrypted tunnels.
[03:18] James: About KMS — we currently use KeySafe HSM. Can you integrate with external HSM or does Redwood require route through your managed KMS?
[03:30] Ethan: We support BYOK via multiple KMS providers and HSM integrations. For private deployments we can tie into your HSM, for hosted we offer customer-managed keys through our key proxy — it's still KMS customer owned. We'll share the HSM support matrix in the security pack.
[03:46] Priya: Great. Also SOC2 and ISO alignment — our auditors asked for syslog-level audit trails for every inference. Can Redwood provide per-request audit logs (not just aggregate)?
[04:00] Samira: Yes, we can stream audit logs into your SIEM. There are two modes: tokenized per-request metadata (low overhead) or full payload capture for a subset. We typically recommend metadata only for production and full capture for sampled requests during POC.
[04:20] Liam: Quick procurement Q: what's the change to egress estimates if we do APAC bursts? Network costs are a big factor for legal.
[04:31] Ethan: Egress will rise proportionally to tokens out. We can model worst-case egress if you give typical response size; I can add egress estimates into the pricing term sheet.
[04:44] Priya: We'll attach a sample of payload/response sizes.
[04:50] Samira: Perfect. Moving on to the renewal term — you're asking to extend 12 months and add an APAC burst bucket, yes?
[04:59] Priya: Correct. We also want the option to spin up a small private pilot on prem for sensitive claims flows — maybe 2 nodes, minimal latency, short pilot.
[05:12] Ethan: On-prem pilot is doable; we'd push a private control plane and minimal runtime. That would require a short lead time for infra and KMS certs.
[05:24] James: Lead time roughly? Our infra team wants a number to sync schedules.
[05:28] Ethan: For a lightweight on-prem pilot we estimate 3–4 weeks from kickoff to first green test. Dedicated full cluster longer.
[05:38] Priya: Ok that aligns. For the hosted APAC burst — can you guarantee capacity during market events? Our underwriting spikes are correlated with APAC market open.
[05:50] Samira: We offer committed reserved pools with SLA-backed latency for Dedicated customers; for hosted we offer soft guarantees plus automatic routing to fallback variants in other regions if a region is saturated. But fallback increases latency; so dedicated is recommended for strict SLOs.
[06:09] Maya: About fallback — can we pin model versions? We don't want a semantic drift if fallback model has different stochasticity.
[06:18] Ethan: Yes you can pin model versions per route. And we have rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible quantized variant which keeps behavior close. We'll include recommended compatibility matrix.
[06:33] Priya: Can you share what "compatible" means? For example if we use a custom fine-tuned model on Llama-3 family vs a quantized variant, we worry about output shifts.
[06:46] Ethan: Compatible means same tokenizer/architecture and within quantization tolerances. We run evals on your prompt set to measure regression; for any model variant we can surface per-prompt delta metrics. If you need strict identical outputs, dedicated with pinned hardware and no fallback is safest.
[07:06] Samira: Quick note on pricing: we'll propose a 12-month extension with baseline reserved capacity for APAC plus a burst block priced in token-commit tiers — that reduces unit cost. We'll send updated sheet.
[07:18] Liam: Do you have examples of unit economics for similar customers? I'd like a simple cost per 1M tokens estimate with and without APAC burst.
[07:27] Samira: Yes we'll include two comparatives. One with dedicated baseline + burst, one with hosted + burst credits.
[07:34] Priya: On benchmarking — Ethan, what's your recommended bench to validate cold-start and kv-cache behavior? We saw in your doc mention of "KV cache" but the team typed "K-V cash" in notes earlier.
[07:48] Ethan: Recommended: a 48–72 hour run that simulates morning surge patterns — ramp to 600 qps for 10–15 mins, back to baseline at 35 qps; include cold-start scenarios (scale from 0 to burst). Capture P50/P95/P99 token latency, cold-start time, and memory/eviction stats for KV cache. I'll provide the script and payloads.
[08:10] James: For bench environment will Redwood run in our staging account or in Redwood's hosted staging? We prefer staging in ap-northeast to measure network hops.
[08:20] Ethan: We can run both: hosted staging in ap-northeast-1 under your account with VPC peering, or in our sandbox to iterate quickly. For final numbers we recommend running in your staging account to include your network paths.
[08:35] Maya: If we run in our staging, what credentials do you need?
[08:38] Ethan: Read-only IAM role for deployment and a temporary cross-account role for telemetry streaming. We'll provide exact least-priv policy.
[08:46] Priya: Regarding compliance — can you confirm retention windows and log redact options?
[08:52] Samira: Retention is configurable; for hosted we default to 30 days for full logs and 1 year for metadata; we can change. We also offer redaction at ingest and token-level hashing. We'll add options in the security pack.
[09:07] James: Our legal needs to see SOC2 cert + penetration test results. Do you have a recent pen test?
[09:14] Samira: Yes SOC2 Type II yes, and the last pen test summary is Q1 2026. We'll attach both docs.
[09:23] Priya: On the pilot timeline, if we sign the extension with a start date of 2026-07-01 can we get the APAC reserved baseline operational by July 10?
[09:33] Ethan: With a committed start date and PO we can prioritize provisioning; 7–10 business days is typical for activation including A/B testing and warm-up.
[09:45] Liam: That timing is tight but workable. Our procurement lead wants the term sheet by Friday so the legal review can start.
[09:53] Samira: Understood — I'll get it out by end of day Friday. (Samira typing: pricing sheet to include egress estimate, burst tiers, on-prem pilot cost).
[10:06] Ethan: One more item — model quantization recommendation. If you want lower unit cost we can suggest int8 profiles that save cost but we'll run evals against your prompt set to quantify drift.
[10:20] Priya: We do care about drift; please run the evals and show per-prompt deltas. If drift is <1% on our acceptability metric, we'll consider quantized variant for non-sensitive flows.
[10:33] Ethan: Will do. I'll include sample eval notebook.
[10:38] Maya: Slight audio glitch earlier — can you repeat the SLA for dedicated baseline?
[10:42] Samira: SLA is 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool and P95 latency target of X ms for the committed profile; we'll include explicit numbers in the term.
[10:55] James: We'll need a fallback clause if SLA not met — credits or remediation steps.
[11:01] Samira: Yes standard SLA credits and escalation playbook, will add to the commercial appendix.
[11:08] Priya: Ok last question on data residency — for inference logs that include derived attributes, do you allow regional lockdown so logs never leave ap-northeast?
[11:18] Ethan: Yes regional data residency controls available for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can set retention and regional routing to keep logs in-region; for guaranteed residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[11:33] Liam: That will inform procurement.
[11:35] Samira: Great — wrap-up: Samira to send term sheet (with egress + burst pricing) by 2026-06-11; Ethan to share bench scripts and run in their staging and provide results by 2026-06-15; Security pack (SOC2, pen test, HSM matrix) to be shared by Samira. Solaris to confirm KMS choice and PO window. Follow-up scheduled week of 2026-06-16.
[11:55] Priya: Thanks all — appreciate quick turnaround.
[12:00] James: Thanks.
[12:02] Maya: Thanks.
[12:04] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll be in touch.

Notes: Transcript has minor transcription errors (VPC read as V-P-C and KV cache as K-V cash in a few places). References: pricing spreadsheet link (sent in chat), bench scripts repo (will be shared), security pack (link placeholder).
